Thank you, Madam Chair. Good morning. My name is Angela Gardner, General Manager, Utilities Environment Division. The first item today deals with a done Donald Avenue Solar Farm project.
Committee received a report on this project at its April meeting indicated that a scope reduction would be necessary in order to keep the project within the original budget limits.
The project indicated that it was possible to reduce the scope by installing fewer solar panels while leaving opportunities for future expansion.
The report outlined the significant environmental benefits and the alignment of the project with the city's low emissions community plan.

Last month, committee resolved that the administration will report back with options to pursue a second phase of the project at the original to restore the original scope of power generation or full utilization of the site, including full payback costing analysis and exploration of reserve funding as well as internal loans for the project.
This report provides committee with three options for consideration. The options are summarized in the table on page five of the report.
Just a brief overview of these options option one aligns with the existing budget for the project and would be located at the north end of the site as shown on the plan.
This option would generate 1.06 megawatts of electricity and would be designed to accommodate future expansion for the entire site.
The total cost for this option is 4.39 million which is currently fully funded.
Option two would involve the installation of additional solar panels in order to generate 2.23 megawatts of electricity and would extend further south on the site.
Again, this option would be designed to ultimately allow future expansion. The total cost for this option is 6.23 million dollars.

In order to proceed with this option, it would be necessary to allocate an additional 1.8 million dollars to the project from the electrical distribution extension reserve, which is one of the utility.

The sustainability reserves. Although there is still a significant asset management funding gap for Saskatoon light and power, this investment would provide long-term financial benefits by reducing bulk energy costs from Sask power.
The third option involves the development of the entire site with solar panels generating 3.09 megawatts of electricity.
The total cost for this option is 8.46 million. This would require 4.07 million of additional funding.
Proposed funding for this option would include the 1.84 million from Saskatoon light and power capital reserves as I mentioned as well as 2.23 million dollars from borrowing.
The payback period for options 1 and 2 would be 13 years and the payback period for option 3 would be 16 years in order to account for the internal cost for borrowing.

The administration is recommending option 3 which is the full implementation of all the phases. This option provides a positive financial return on investment and maximizes the environmental benefits.
Although there are options to stage construction over time, option 3 does provide the lowest cost option for construction.
